name: Complex Discharge Dictation
description: Comprehensive discharge dictation covering diagnosis, medications, procedures, and follow-up

transcript.rawText: 65 year old male patient admitted with acute coronary syndrome underwent primary PCI with drug eluting stent placement to left anterior descending artery. Procedure was uncomplicated. Principal diagnosis is acute ST elevation myocardial infarction. Secondary diagnoses include hypertension dyslipidemia and smoker. During the hospital stay patient was started on dual antiplatelet therapy with Aspirin 75 milligrams once daily and Clopidogrel 75 milligrams once daily for 12 months. Also started on Metoprolol 25 milligrams twice daily for heart rate control and blood pressure. Atorvastatin 80 milligrams at bedtime continued. Ramipril 2.5 milligrams once daily started for LV function improvement. Patient was counseled on lifestyle modifications including smoking cessation dietary changes and regular exercise. Discharge medications include Aspirin Clopidogrel Metoprolol Atorvastatin Ramipril and Pantoprazole 40 milligrams once daily for gastric protection. Patient to follow up with cardiology after 1 month and with cardiologist after 1 week for wound check. Echocardiogram showed LV ejection fraction 45 percent with mild hypokinesia of inferior wall. No signs of heart failure. Patient is stable for discharge in good condition.
